div.head: Hn 36.1a
div.ab: Nemo enim ouerseunessam sui ipsius habet, set fortasse dominus eius.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 566 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: 36, 1a erklärt, wieso Overseunessa häufig von Rechtswegen nicht existirt; ebenso 24, 1. Zu Nemo schreibt Corr. an den Rand: su. e . C . [d. h. sumitur e contra?] super barones Sc; genau so roth am Rande Hg

36, 1a explains why the overseunessa frequently does not exist by right; similarly 24, 1. Beside Nemo the corrector writes in the margin: su. e . C . [i.e. sumitur e contra?] super barones Sc; exactly the same in red in the margin Hg

div.ab: For no one has the ouerseunesse of himself, but perhaps his lord.
